title: 80B tokens later…
author: 00G_WAY
selftext: I’m roughly 80B tokens deep into my dream game (don’t worry artists, I’m a visual artist and am hand-drawing 100% of the textures. Claude is for code). I will be releasing a free demo at the February Steam Next Fest. BUT I was just scrolling the indiegamedev reddit page and noticed someone saying that he’s released 3 games, all of which were heavily AI aided, and did not disclose the AI support to Steam. And he made over $100,000 profit. Is this normal? His excuse was that it was unfair to lose sales on account of blind anti-AI hate. Like… i see the point? But also, like, if the game is good, then using AI shouldn’t change that. Is it reasonable to lie to Steam in the wake of AI-use discrimination? Or is it more reasonable to just make a dope game and be honest about AI? To be clear, I don’t have the cajones to lie to Steam about this—nor would I want to. My game is a passion project that I am doing because I love games, not because I am hoping to profit. I just wanted to see how people are thinking about AI disclosure in the wake of AI slop after 500+ claude-supported commits.

comments.author: Morpegom
comments.body:
What do you mean? AI tag on steam is for visual and assets that the player sees on screen. You can't lie about that, they are going to eventually report you.

Depending on the case the game can be removed from steam, sales revoked or free refunds for people who wants it.

It is not required for coding assisting no. Vibecoded games is another story I think.

Keep in mind tho that if the AI wrote a visible description for you or it made the interface thats still counts for the tag.
